subject: Day 19: sustained eye contact emerging; pediatrician prep
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 19. Sustained eye contact during feeds is emerging if not already. First social smile (in response to a face, not a reflex) typically appears between week 4 and week 6, so any day now through day 42. Pediatrician will look for it at the 1-month visit.

Action items
- Pre-write your questions for the 1-month visit. Items to cover: weight curve, jaundice resolution, feeding pattern, sleep stretches, maternal mood, vaccine schedule for the 2-month visit. AAP Bright Futures parent handout for 1-month: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- Schedule a maternal 6-week postpartum visit with the OB for around day 42 if not already booked. ACOG on the postpartum period: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-pain-management
- Continue daycare or nanny waitlist research. ChildCare.gov directory: https://www.childcare.gov/
- If considering swaddle-to-sleep-sack transition timing, the rule of thumb is to stop swaddling before signs of rolling (typically week 8-12). AAP HealthyChildren on safe sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/A-Parents-Guide-to-Safe-Sleep.aspx
- Continue feeding log.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Brief head lifts in tummy time. Hands sometimes opening. Sustained eye contact during feeds. Some early cooing or non-cry sounds.
- [low concern] Cradle cap (yellow scale on scalp) emerging — common, harmless, resolves over weeks.
- [monitor] Crying more than 3 hours per day for 3+ days could indicate colic — peaks 6-8 weeks, resolves by 12-16 weeks. AAP HealthyChildren on crying: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/crying-colic/Pages/default.aspx
- [call within 24h] Forceful projectile vomiting + weight loss (pyloric stenosis presents weeks 3-6). Fewer than six wet diapers per day.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C). Lethargy, refusal of all feeds, blue or grey color, breathing faster than 60 per minute at rest, persistent grunting, projectile or bilious-green vomiting. Apnea (>20 sec pause or with color change). Seizure-like activity. Call 911 for blue lips or unresponsiveness!

Enrichment opportunity
Face-to-face talking during awake-alert windows: hold Avi 8-12 inches from your face and talk slowly with exaggerated facial expressions. He prefers human faces over other patterns and is starting to recognize parental voices.

Upcoming
- Day 28-35: 1-month well visit window opens; first social smiles begin.
- Day 35-42: peak PURPLE crying curve at about 6 weeks.
- Day 42: maternal 6-week postpartum visit (clearance for exercise and intimacy).
- Day 60: 2-month well visit; first round of vaccines.

Further reading
- AAP HealthyChildren on safe sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/A-Parents-Guide-to-Safe-Sleep.aspx
- AAP HealthyChildren on crying and colic: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/crying-colic/Pages/default.aspx
- AAP Bright Futures periodicity schedule: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/
- ACOG on the postpartum period: https://www.acog.org/womens-health/faqs/postpartum-pain-management

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Calms when picked up or spoken to
  AAP window: day 14-60
  What to look for: Early co-regulation. Not the same as stopping crying immediately — look for any shift in state.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/calms-with-soothing/complete

- Briefly lifts head during tummy time
  AAP window: day 14-60
  What to look for: Few seconds of head lift, even with bobble, counts. Builds neck strength for later head control.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/brief-head-lift/complete

- Quiets or turns toward a familiar voice
  AAP window: day 7-45
  What to look for: Voice recognition begins before birth; postnatally it shows as orienting or settling to a parent's voice.
  Source: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/Pages/Developmental-Milestones-1-Month.aspx
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/recognizes-parent-voice/complete

- Watches your face when you talk
  AAP window: day 7-60
  What to look for: Baseline social orientation. Look for sustained gaze, even briefly, during alert windows.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/tracks-face-briefly/complete

- Moves both arms and both legs
  AAP window: day 0-60
  What to look for: Symmetric, spontaneous movement of all four limbs. Asymmetry warrants pediatric attention.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/moves-arms-and-legs/complete
